name: Elliott Smith
label: Kill Rock Stars
lede: A four-track tape made in a Portland basement for a seven-inch single ends up at the Oscars, then on a major label, and then in the catalogue of one of the most closely loved songwriters of his era.

eras.title: A Nebraska kid finds Portland
eras.text: Steven Paul Smith is born in Omaha, grows up in Texas and lands in Portland as a teenager. By the time he leaves Hampshire College with a philosophy degree, he has already met the guitarist who will help start his first real band.

years.h: Steven Paul Smith is born in Omaha, Nebraska
years.p: His parents split when he was six months old, and he grew up in Duncanville, Texas, with his mother. He started piano at nine and guitar at ten, per Wikipedia.

years.h: He moves to Portland to live with his father
years.p: At 14 Smith goes to Portland, Oregon, and later graduates from Lincoln High School as a National Merit Scholar. He plays in school-era bands under pseudonyms, including Stranger Than Fiction and A Murder of Crows.

years.h: Hampshire College: a philosophy degree and a bandmate
years.p: Smith graduates from Hampshire College in Amherst, Massachusetts, with a degree in philosophy and political science. There he plays with [[Neil Gust|22b82975-a4ef-4110-b968-67f753edfdfa]] in a band called Swimming Jesus, and the two move to Portland.
years.xp: Per Wikipedia, his senior thesis was titled "Toward a Post-Structuralist Feminist Jurisprudence." The Kierkegaard book that later gave Either/Or its title comes from the same philosophy background.

eras.title: Loud band by day, four-track at night
eras.text: Smith fronts Heatmiser in Portland's clubs while quietly making solo tapes on a four-track. One of those tapes turns into a record by accident, and Kill Rock Stars follows.

years.h: [[Heatmiser|99a18561-8a7d-4c30-8d3b-31bdf8c4b8ed]] forms in Portland
years.p: [[Neil Gust|22b82975-a4ef-4110-b968-67f753edfdfa]], Tony Lash and Brandt Peterson join Elliott Smith in a loud guitar band that becomes a fixture at the X-Ray Cafe and La Luna.
years.xp: Per Wikipedia, Heatmiser released Dead Air (1993) and Cop and Speeder (1994) on Frontier Records, plus the Yellow No. 5 EP in 1994. Manager JJ Gonson recalled that $300 for a show was "huge" in 1993.

years.h: Roman Candle is taped on a four-track in a basement
years.p: Smith records every instrument himself in the basement of JJ Gonson, his girlfriend and Heatmiser's manager. He uses a Shure SM57 and a cheap RadioShack mic.
years.xp: He expected only a 7-inch single to come of it. Gonson played the tape for Cavity Search Records, and the label wanted the whole thing.

q: At the time it was so opposite to the grunge thing.
years.src: Wikipedia: Roman Candle · Wikipedia: Elliott Smith · Wikipedia: Cavity Search Records
years.h: A 7-inch single becomes a whole album: Roman Candle
years.p: Cavity Search Records owner Christopher Cooper asks for the full four-track tape instead. Roman Candle comes out on CD and cassette.
years.xp:
Cavity Search, a Portland label whose roster also included [[Pete Krebs|5985db1d-8a83-4c3c-993a-e0f589c2e24d]] and Heatmiser, put the record out. Smith hesitated before agreeing. Domino issued it on vinyl in the UK in 1998, and Kill Rock Stars reissued it in 2010.

Smith later described how out of step it felt with its moment.

years.h: [[Sam Coomes|36a1dddb-41b3-4ab7-bc1e-973540a9e2eb]] takes over bass in Heatmiser
years.p: Brandt Peterson, who played on Heatmiser's first two records, leaves in August 1994. Coomes, later of [[Quasi|3df29542-402a-49a5-ae1f-82f936184b3b]], plays on the last Heatmiser album.
years.xp: Smith later called removing Peterson painful, comparing it to breaking up with somebody, per Wikipedia's Heatmiser article.

years.h: Mary Lou Lord hears him and points him to Slim Moon
years.p: Lord sees Smith play in Seattle, takes him on tour, and introduces him to [[Slim Moon|602432a1-35ce-40ef-90e8-c4a123d438bf]] of Kill Rock Stars.
years.xp: Moon recalled being so struck by Smith's set that he went out to the tour van to listen to his CD for the rest of the show, per Consequence.

years.h: Elliott Smith: first record on Kill Rock Stars
years.p: Tracked at Tony Lash's house and at Leslie Uppinghouse's house, it includes "Needle in the Hay". The cover is JJ Gonson's photo of a sculpture of two figures falling.
years.xp: Moon said the album was not well received when it came out. It sold well in Portland but struggled nationally, per Consequence. Wes Anderson later used "Needle in the Hay" in The Royal Tenenbaums (2001).

eras.title: Heatmiser ends, Either/Or begins
eras.text: The band Smith started with a college friend dissolves right as it signs to a big label. The solo record he finishes that year is the one that reaches Hollywood.

years.h: Heatmiser's last record, and the band ends
years.p: Mic City Sons comes out on Caroline with Sam Coomes on bass. Heatmiser dissolves in fall 1996, with Tony Lash out before the final tour and John Moen in on drums.
years.xp: Neil Gust recalled that Smith "drifted into his own thing" as his solo career grew, per Wikipedia. Smith later said he regretted criticizing Heatmiser in solo interviews and believed it hurt Gust.

years.h: Either/Or: the record with the Kierkegaard title
years.p: Recorded in 1995-96 around Portland, including [[Joanna Bolme|21f4bc79-8b24-4aee-85b3-22f46cf2e5d2]]'s house, with [[Tom Rothrock|73092a6a-9821-419c-9638-484487d55927]] and [[Rob Schnapf|e223c819-4a5d-4bd1-b7e6-21888f145b55]] mixing most of it. It includes "Between the Bars".
years.xp: Smith played every instrument and mixed several tracks himself, per Wikipedia. Kill Rock Stars issued a remastered Expanded Edition in 2017 under Larry Crane's supervision.

years.cap: Joanna Bolme of Stephen Malkmus & the Jicks performing at the Constellations... · Wikimedia
years.h: [[Gus Van Sant|c41bf429-3f3d-4d5c-95c6-a3afb6831146]] falls for Either/Or
years.p: Van Sant licenses three Smith songs for Good Will Hunting and commissions a new one, "Miss Misery".
years.xp: Per Wikipedia, the soundtrack also has an orchestral version of "Between the Bars" recorded with Danny Elfman. Van Sant later used another Either/Or track in Paranoid Park (2007).

years.h: "Miss Misery" is recorded at Jackpot with Larry Crane
years.p: Smith cuts the song at Jackpot! Recording Studio in Portland, run by his friend Larry Crane. An earlier version with different words later appears on New Moon.

eras.title: A white suit and a major label
eras.text: An Oscar nomination drags a Portland songwriter onto national television, and DreamWorks signs him. The record he makes next is his most produced yet.

q: It was fun to walk around on the moon for a day.
years.src: Slate · Wikipedia: Miss Misery · Wikipedia: 70th Academy Awards
years.h: The Oscars: a white suit and one song
years.p: Nominated for Best Original Song, Smith performs "Miss Misery" live at the Academy Awards. "My Heart Will Go On" from Titanic wins.
years.xp:
Smith agreed to play only after producers said the song would be performed with or without him. Slate reports he wore a white sport coat with a pink carnation and performed about 90 seconds between Aaliyah and Céline Dion. He arrived with producer [[Rob Schnapf|e223c819-4a5d-4bd1-b7e6-21888f145b55]], manager Margaret Mittleman and girlfriend [[Joanna Bolme|21f4bc79-8b24-4aee-85b3-22f46cf2e5d2]].

He described the night as surreal.

years.h: Smith signs with DreamWorks Records
years.p: He leaves Kill Rock Stars for DreamWorks Records, his first major-label deal, while living in Brooklyn.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates the signing to 1998. XO is his only album to be released in his lifetime on DreamWorks besides Figure 8.

years.h: XO: strings, horns and a bigger studio
years.p: Smith tracks it in Los Angeles at Sunset Sound and other studios with [[Rob Schnapf|e223c819-4a5d-4bd1-b7e6-21888f145b55]] and [[Tom Rothrock|73092a6a-9821-419c-9638-484487d55927]], after early demos at Jackpot. "Waltz #2 (XO)" is the single.
years.xp: Its working title was "Grand Mal". [[Jon Brion|a32e4aac-1db8-4dc6-be34-a813c4530627]] and drummer Joey Waronker contribute. Per Wikipedia, his 1998 touring band included [[Quasi|3df29542-402a-49a5-ae1f-82f936184b3b]]'s Sam Coomes and Janet Weiss.

years.h: Saturday Night Live: "Waltz #2 (XO)" with a full band
years.p: Smith plays the song with John Moen, [[Jon Brion|a32e4aac-1db8-4dc6-be34-a813c4530627]], Rob Schnapf and [[Sam Coomes|36a1dddb-41b3-4ab7-bc1e-973540a9e2eb]] behind him.

eras.title: Silver Lake and a stalled fourth record
eras.text: Smith moves to Los Angeles, makes his most polished record, and then the sessions for what would be his next one start to come apart.

years.h: Brooklyn out, Silver Lake in
years.p: Smith relocates from Brooklyn to Los Angeles and plays small acoustic shows at places like the Silverlake Lounge.

years.h: He covers the Beatles' "Because" for American Beauty
years.p: Smith's version of "Because" appears on the American Beauty soundtrack.

years.h: Figure 8: Abbey Road, and a Beatles-sized ambition
years.p: Recorded 1998-99 at Sunset Sound, Capitol and Sonora in Los Angeles and at Abbey Road in London, with Rothrock and Schnapf. "Son of Sam" opens it.
years.xp: Per Wikipedia it was his last album released in his lifetime, and it charted higher than anything else he put out while alive.

years.cap: Photo: Autumn de Wilde, cover shoot
years.h: The ugliest mural on Sunset Boulevard becomes the cover
years.p: Photographer Autumn de Wilde shoots Smith in front of a wall on Sunset Boulevard in Silver Lake. It becomes a fan memorial.
years.xp: De Wilde told LAist she took Polaroids of murals along Sunset and picked what she called "the ugliest mural I'd ever seen." She wanted Smith to look unaware of the color behind him.

years.h: Songs with Jon Brion stall, and the friendship ends
years.p: Sessions for a next record with [[Jon Brion|a32e4aac-1db8-4dc6-be34-a813c4530627]] are abandoned, and the two stop speaking.
years.xp: Wikipedia says Smith developed a heroin addiction after the Figure 8 tour and tried rehab, and that Brion's concerns over his substance use ended the sessions. Wikipedia also says he showed paranoia and believed a white van was following him.

years.h: Smith and Neil Gust record one last song together
years.p: The pair cut "Who's Behind the Door?" for Gust's band No. 2, the last time the two Heatmiser founders record together.

years.h: Smith is arrested at a Flaming Lips and Beck show
years.p: Per Wikipedia, Los Angeles police beat and arrest him at a concert with the Flaming Lips and [[Beck|309c62ba-7a22-4277-9f67-4a162526d18a]], injuring his back and forcing cancellations.

eras.title: The last year
eras.text: A run of sold-out solo shows, a sober spring and summer, and a fifth album he did not finish.

years.h: Two sold-out nights at the Henry Fonda Theater
years.p: Smith plays solo acoustic in Hollywood on January 31 and February 1, an attempt to reset.

years.h: Last show: Redfest at the University of Utah
years.p: Smith closes the set at Salt Lake City with the Beatles' "Long, Long, Long".

years.h: Smith dies at 34 in Los Angeles
years.p: He died of two stab wounds to the chest at his Echo Park home. A coroner's spokesman said the trauma could have been self-inflicted or inflicted by another, and no determination was made.
years.xp:
Per Wikipedia, girlfriend Jennifer Chiba said the two were arguing before she locked herself in a bathroom, and that she found him with a knife in his chest. Police first treated it as a suicide, according to Today. The coroner found no illegal substances or alcohol, and the LAPD investigation is listed as open.

His ashes were divided among his mother, father and half-sister.

eras.title: The records that came after
eras.text: Producers, friends and his old label finish and gather what he left, and the songs keep finding new listeners.

years.src: Wikipedia: From a Basement on the Hill
years.h: From a Basement on the Hill: 15 songs from over 30
years.p: Rob Schnapf and Joanna Bolme choose 15 tracks from more than 30 Smith recorded from 2000 to 2003. He had wanted a double album.
years.xp: Schnapf said he felt protective and did not want anyone to mess with it. The album, released by ANTI-, debuted at No. 19 on the Billboard 200, per Wikipedia.

years.h: A plaque goes up at Lincoln High School
years.p: The Portland school he graduated from installs a memorial plaque.

years.h: New Moon: 24 songs from 1994-97 on Kill Rock Stars
years.p: The double-disc collection of songs recorded between 1994 and 1997 debuts at No. 24 on the Billboard 200.

years.h: Heaven Adores You documentary opens
years.p: Nickolas Rossi's film, released by Eagle Rock Entertainment, gets a limited theatrical run.

years.h: Either/Or returns, remastered, with extra songs
years.p: Kill Rock Stars reissues it for its 20th anniversary with Larry Crane supervising the remaster.
years.xp: Willamette Week noted unreleased material including "I Figured You Out", originally given to Mary Lou Lord.
